purpose: Drafter exam of F1 (TSK-250 .. TSK-255): how the Coach recommends heroes. Measures; changes nothing. PASS technical != strategic improvement.

data.empiricalPatchAttribution: label-only, UNVERIFIED -- the source reports no patch; the label is applied by our ingestion

positionalDataset.completeness: all observed rows retained (see the file's provenance)

limitations: Frozen statistical snapshot labelled 7.41e (label unverified); curated positions/counters are hand-curated. Absolute numbers are comparative baselines, not truth.
The simulated Player follows V3 (follow-coach / varied / deviate); the Enemy Bot is scripted. States are realistic, not human.

The lab saves no team pools, so POOL_SCARCITY cannot fire: the declared-precedence reference reads the session's own pools/occupancy (R2). R1 approximated pools with the Player's personal pool and invented scarcity (found in the TSK-251 T2 run).
I3 'declared precedence' is LivePositionPriorityV1 evaluated offline over the board's own columns; it does not run in the simulator today.
I11 (honest basis) is measured from TSK-254 on; reports written before it had no `basis` field and say so.

I6 has two rulers: `I6_visible` keeps the ORIGINAL definition of every report up to T4_AFTER; `I6_visible_revised` (TSK-254) applies only with every own pick curated and also reads V4 card risks. Their numbers are not comparable; a drop from one to the other is a change of rule, not an improvement.

M1 / exposure / D1 are counts over the simulator's own states (a scripted rival, a frozen snapshot): they say how often a trade-off exists, never whether it hurts a real game. That is the judge's call.

I6_visible.definition: original (T2..T4_AFTER): an uncurated own pick counts as lacking; only V3/board texts make the gap visible
I6_visible.note: A late open initiation/catch gap that no card mentions. T4/T5 are expected to close it; at baseline it is a known defect.

I6_visible_revised.definition: revised (T5, TSK-254): applies only with every own pick curated; a V4 card risk text also makes the gap visible
I6_visible_revised.note: Smaller denominator than I6_visible by construction. A drop from the original to this one is a change of ruler, NOT an improvement: do not compare the two numbers.

I9_visible.note: Plan v2: allowed in the top-3 only when fewer than 3 credible alternatives exist AND the risk is shown. At baseline the risk is never shown.

I11_honestBasis.note: Every V4 card carries a coherent basis, and it does not contradict its reason (a capability claim is curated, a quoted statistic is statistical). Reports before TSK-254 had no basis (NOT_MEASURABLE).

I6c_criticalGapOnCards.note: CRITICAL_GAP is shown only when the gap is critical (<= 2 own picks left, every own pick curated) and the card's hero is curated and does not fill it; and it is never missing from such a card.

I3_openingOnCore.note: Simulator recommends Pos 1/2 on the Player's first decision of round 1 with no COUNTER_WINDOW/POOL_SCARCITY behind it.

I4_reactivityJaccardTop3.note: 1.0 = the same three heroes for a position in every draft.

I5_positionFitShareOfScore.note: level = share of V6's score that is position_fit; order = cov(position_fit, score)/var(score) among the candidates V6 keeps (TOP_N) for the recommended column. Not the whole credible field: V6 truncates before the exam can see it.

I5_positionFitOverWholeField.note: Whole credible field of the recommended column, scored by V6 and peeled past its TOP_N cut. A fair cut is ~0.5 in the more-played half; 'kept without position_fit' = Jaccard between the real top-k and the top-k of the same scores with position_fit's contribution removed (1 = it decides nothing).

T3_pairedRuleChange.note: Same decision points, two rules. 'Changed' = the set of the top-3 differs. This says WHAT moved, not whether it is better: that is the judge's call (changedDecisions in the judge packet).

I6b_initiation.note: Initiation on its own (TSK-253). The original I6 asks for initiation OR catch: 69% of curated heroes have one of the two, so that union is almost never missing.

T4_closingNeeds.note: Same decision points, same credible field. 'Critical' = initiation / catch / damage_mix open with <= 2 own picks left and every own pick curated. It says what moved and what it gives up under the legacy score; whether it is better is the judge's call.

M1_criticalGapVsAdverseCounter.note: Applicable = a critical gap in the closing window AND a revealed enemy. 'Promoted' = the stage-aware rule has a hero that fills the gap first where the legacy rule had somebody else. 'Adverse' = that hero's STATISTICAL counter against a revealed enemy is at or below the threshold with at least that many games, and no curated hard counter (RB-4 demotes those). It counts how often the trade-off exists; whether it hurts is the judge's call.

T6_round1ExposureOnCards.note: Cards, not the board's primary (I8): the V4 card is what carries `exposed_to_counter`. `inconsistencies` must be 0: a card with an available curated hard counter always says so in round 1, and never says so without one.

D1_notEvaluable.note: 'Not evaluable' = an own pick or the card's hero has no curated capabilities, so CRITICAL_GAP can neither be raised nor ruled out. The card then shows nothing, which looks the same as 'evaluated, no gap'. No card ever says 'no risk'.

I10_round1Top3InMorePlayedHalf.note: Observation only (plan v2 removed it as a gate): high = the ranking leans on popularity.

componentQuestions.text: Position order: is the position the board recommends the right one to commit to NOW (and not just the lowest open one)?
Hero ranking: are the heroes shown for that position the ones you would consider, or do they look chosen for being popular?
Composition: does the advice notice what the team still lacks (initiation / catch / damage mix)?
Exposure: is any recommended hero a clear counter-target of what the rival has shown, and does the card say so?

planQuestions.text: Does this team need to win early, or can it scale?
Can this draft convert an advantage into objectives?
Does the recommendation improve the plan, or only the score?
